Announcement.Title: The new iNELS website is live
Announcement.Content: The new iNELS website brings solutions, industries, products, downloads and support for homes, hotels and commercial buildings together in one place. It also covers open integrations such as KNX, BACnet, Modbus, MQTT and the major voice assistants, along with reference projects and an installer finder.

Announcement.Title: iNELS Harmony manual on the wiki
Announcement.Content: The iNELS Harmony user manual is now available on the wiki. Harmony combines room control with hotel operations such as reservations, check-in, keys and housekeeping, in three web apps running on one on-site server. The guide is organised by role, so installers, reception staff and housekeepers each start from their own section.

Announcement.Title: All iNELS newsletters in one place
Announcement.Content: Every iNELS newsletter is now collected on a single wiki page, newest first. Product launches, iDM releases and application notes sent out since 2024 are easy to find again and share with customers.

Announcement.Title: Linking central units over Modbus IP
Announcement.Content: A new iDM3 tutorial shows how to link iNELS central units over Modbus IP, so a button on one CU can switch an output on another. It walks through planning the register map, setting up the master and slave sides, and a step-by-step test sequence for tracking down faults.

Announcement.Title: Hotel-Room Object documented
Announcement.Content: The Hotel-Room Object now has a full step-by-step guide on the wiki. It gathers occupancy, DND, MUR, climate, HVAC and scenes for a guest room into one virtual device with a single MQTT topic for PMS and BMS integration. Rooms only appear in iNELS Harmony once this object is added, so include it from the start on hospitality projects.

Announcement.Title: iDM3 checks for firmware updates
Announcement.Content: iDM3 checks for published device firmware on every launch and offers newer versions on the unit that needs them. Downloading before going on site is still worth doing – connectivity in plant rooms is unreliable.
